APIDiscoveryResponse.description: Public service identity, never a robot connection or authorization credential.
APIDiscoveryResponse.title: APIDiscoveryResponse

ts.description: when the action really happened (default: now). Never in the future; lets a call be logged after the fact

ActivityCardResult.description: What the device returns for `suggest_activity`. shown=false: a card is already up, or they said no before.
ActivityCardResult.title: ActivityCardResult

AgentStep.description: One step the cloud really ran to build this insight. Counts and categories only; never record content.

items.description: how many records / findings / nodes this step handled

AgentStep.title: AgentStep

AgreedActivity.description:
One activity the person said yes to in a conversation, held by the cloud for that local day so every
screen shows the same thing (tool `agree_activity`). `text` is a template from config/voice_lines.toml
(`voice_key`) around the activity's name and where it was agreed: never the person's words. It becomes
`done` by itself when an observation for that activity arrives the same day; a device reports `started`
(opened) or `put_aside` with POST /v1/me/agreed/answer. Gone after local midnight.

day.description: the local day it belongs to; it is not shown on any other day

id.description: send it back in the answer; also the id in the stream's `agreed` events

line.description: Kaiku's own short line from the conversation, when it gave one and it passed the wording rules

name.description: how the activity is called on a screen ("Lantern", "a walk")

on.description: the person's screens that can open it

opens_here.description: the asking device (`surface` in the query) has a screen for it; false: show it without an open button

state_at.description: when it was opened, done or put aside

text.description: the sentence for the card and the notification

voice_key.description: the template used; speak `text` with POST /v1/voice/say

when.description: now: they want to do it now, on another device. later: some time today

AgreedActivity.title: AgreedActivity

AgreedAnswer.description:
POST /v1/me/agreed/answer — opened: this device opened the activity's screen (state started). put_aside:
the person put it aside (final for today). Done needs no answer: the activity's own observation does it.
AgreedAnswer.title: AgreedAnswer

AgreedResult.description:
Result of the `agree_activity` tool when the yes was kept. A refusal is `ok=false` with `error` (a reason
the model can say) and `result {agreed: false, reason}`; nothing is stored then.

already.description: this activity was already agreed and open today: nothing new was added

listening.description: screens whose app is open right now (the stream is connected): it appeared there this second. The others show it when the app is next opened

on.description: the person's screens that now show it and can open it

where.description: say it this way: "your phone and your Mac"

AgreedResult.title: AgreedResult

metrics.description: criteria metric names this sentence rests on

CareSharing.description:
GET/PUT /v1/me/sharing — the person's choice to show their care team what Kaiku has learned (the knowledge
graph and routines from conversations). Default off (D34). People, places, likes and plans are never shared.
CareSharing.title: CareSharing

ChatShape.description: How this conversation should run, for the device: the same guidance the model reads in its instruction.
ChatShape.title: ChatShape

ClinicianBrief.description:
GET /v1/patients/{id}/brief — weekly clinician brief (flagship, grounded in metric ids; template fallback).
Explains the consensus; never changes it.
ClinicianBrief.title: ClinicianBrief

purpose.description: why the conversation was opened. check_in: a small passing chat alongside the periodic check-in (see chat_shape). Omitted = today's behaviour for the intent

resume_session_id.description: reuse an open session belonging to this home and surface

walk_style.description: with purpose walk: quiet (mostly listens), playful (one small game at a time) or chatty (keeps a gentle conversation going). Omitted = config/kaiku.toml [walk].default_style

CompanionSessionResponse.description:
POST /v1/companion/session — everything a device needs to open Gemini Live as Kaiku. `live_token` is null
when Live is unavailable: the device reports unavailability and keeps the microphone closed.

chat_shape.description: present when the request named a purpose

context_refresh_seconds.description: poll interval for consented source updates during an active conversation

idle_end_s.description: the device ends the conversation by itself after this long with nobody speaking (an open microphone in a pocket); longer on a walk

live_setup.description: Kaiku's recommended Live BidiGenerateContentSetup (REST camelCase; the token locks only the model): model, voice, system instruction, tools, automatic VAD + barge-in, transcriptions. Send it as the first frame {setup: live_setup}; clients must apply this complete setup.

walk.description: present when the purpose is walk

CompanionSessionResponse.title: CompanionSessionResponse

behavior.description: Live asynchronous function calling: declare it so and answer with the result's `scheduling`

CompanionToolResult.description:
`ok=false` + `error` when the call was refused (not on this surface, bad args, memory rule). `crisis=true`:
a crisis phrase was in the arguments — nothing was stored, obs.safety_flag was raised; stop the session and
show/say `result.script` verbatim. `executor=device`: the device performs the effect itself.
CompanionToolResult.title: CompanionToolResult

simulated.description: the record contains simulated observations (provenance flag; never written into headline or text)

ConstellationResponse.description:
GET /v1/me/constellation — person-facing "Your constellation": people, places, activities, what helps.
Built from what the person told Kaiku and what they did. Never health data, scores or states.
ConstellationResponse.title: ConstellationResponse

agreed.description: activities they said yes to today on any device and whether each is done (D50); each is carried once per state, so Kaiku is glad or asks gently once

chat_depth.description: check-in sessions: how the chat should open

first_name.description: only if the person told Kaiku their name

focus.description: today's focus, chosen by the daily reflection from fixed options

open_items.description: check-in sessions: dials not answered today; at most one is woven into the chat

open_thread.description: topic left open on any surface

outdoor_likes.description: walk sessions: outdoor things and places the person told Kaiku they like, in their words (notebook)

purpose.description: set when the device said why it opened the session

quieter_in.description: today's tasks in which the face signs counted with their opt-in were clearly below their own usual (D52, rule in mind/face_cue.py). An enum and nothing else: the instruction turns it into a cue to go gently and never to mention their face or a camera; no number, no state and no word about how they looked ever crosses

recent_reflection.description: how the latest reflection with Kaiku went, as a level and themes only (never the words), so Kaiku can be gentle about it

source_context.description: prepared source-labelled activity facts; no clinical metrics or raw content

today_facts.description: plain facts the person recorded themselves today, in everyday words ("a short night"); never a number or a judgement

walk_style.description: walk sessions: how Kaiku walks with them

Course.description:
How the record has moved against the person's own usual: what moved first, what followed, what has come
back, what has not. Temporal order only, never a cause. Computed by code from the daily series.

back.description: of those, how many are back within usual

low_date.description: the day most measures were away from usual

moved.description: measures that moved away from usual in this spell

Course.title: Course

CourseEvent.description: One dated point in the course of change. Text, dates and numbers are written by code.
CourseEvent.title: CourseEvent

CriteriaPreview.description: Who would change state under the candidate criteria (nothing is saved).

eval.description: simulation under the candidate, if requested

CriteriaPreview.title: CriteriaPreview

CriteriaResponse.description: GET /v1/admin/criteria — the criteria in effect (file default, or a live override).
CriteriaResponse.title: CriteriaResponse

CriteriaUpdate.description: PUT /v1/admin/criteria (apply) and POST /v1/admin/criteria/preview (dry run). criteria=None resets to file.
CriteriaUpdate.title: CriteriaUpdate

baseline_ready.description: at least one measure has a personal baseline

day_of_record.description: calendar days since the first observation

early_baseline.description: baselines in use are provisional (young record)

simulated.description: the record contains simulated observations (envelope sim flag); the same value as Consensus.simulated and RecordCitation.simulated; per-type counts show how many

DayAccount.description:
One day in plain words, built by code from every source: what was done, what was away from usual, how the
reflection went (level and themes only, when shared).
DayAccount.title: DayAccount

days.description: days the baseline is made from

early.description: provisional baseline of a young record

spread.description: max(1.4826 x MAD, min_mad): what one z unit is

by_code.description: inside a Gemma read: this line is code's own, put there because the model left the measure out or its sentence failed a check

cites.description: DebugFact ids (the model is asked for six at most)

changed.description: by code: what differs from the day before

raw_state.description: what the rule gives for that day alone, before hysteresis

reasons.description: by code: why the rule gives this state

DebugConversation.description: One companion conversation that started that day. Never transcripts, topics or words.

billed_minutes.description: Live minutes the budget ledger counts for it

outcome.description: how it ended; null = never closed

tools.description: tool names: in call order while the conversation is open, one of each once the device has uploaded it

tools_in_order.description: true = `tools` is the call order (repeats kept); false = the device's upload replaced it with one of each, sorted by name; null = cannot be told (a conversation uploaded before this was recorded)

DebugConversation.title: DebugConversation

DebugDay.description:
GET /v1/debug/day?home_id=&date=&generate= — everything about one local day of one home, for developers.
Not for a practitioner and never for the person. Closed like /v1/admin on a deployed service. `generate`
defaults to false: a plain GET never calls a model; `generate=true` asks for Gemma's read of the day.

day_end.description: local midnight that ends it, in UTC

day_start.description: local midnight that starts the day, in UTC

events.description: every stored envelope stamped inside the day, plus a daily summary that measures this day but arrived later; oldest first

first_day.description: the first local day of the home's record (a day picker has nothing before it); null = no record yet

DebugDay.title: DebugDay

DebugEvent.description: One stored envelope of the day.

day.description: the local day this envelope counts toward (a daily summary can be stamped on the day after the one it measures)

payload.description: compact: long lists are cut to their first items plus a count

source.description: the envelope's own source (head, sensors, hub, phone, laptop, glasses, ...)

DebugEvent.title: DebugEvent

DebugFact.description:
One verified line the day read may cite. Ids: metric:<name>, source:<name>, consensus:state,
missing:<source or metric>, tomorrow:<name>, event:<envelope id>.

detail.description: written by code from the day's data; every number in it is the data's

flags.description: the yes/no facts a claim citing this may state, checked like the numbers: held, acknowledged, safety (consensus), enough_data (a signal group), scored (a measure)

numbers.description: the numbers a claim citing this may use

DebugFact.title: DebugFact

DebugFeel.description: One `feel` call: enums only, never what was said.

stance.description: the plan's stance; null for calls stored before it was kept

DebugFeel.title: DebugFeel

DebugMetric.description: One criteria metric on that day, beside its baseline.

beyond_today.description: this day alone is beyond the threshold in the worse direction

flagged.description: counted toward its group's worse weight that day

partial.description: today's running total of a summed or counted measure: shown, but not compared or scored until the day is over (no z)

readings.description: envelopes that day that counted toward it

scored.description: false = observe-only (disabled, weight 0, or criteria role shown): charted, never a vote

scored_days.description: days in the drift window that had a baseline

value.description: the day's value; null = no data that day

worse_z.description: the same, signed so that positive is the worse direction

DebugMetric.title: DebugMetric

cache_hit.description: null: the ledger does not record cache hits

est_usd.description: the spend ledger's estimate for this call, when one row matches it by model, task and time

provider.description: gemini | gemma-hosted | modal | none (a deterministic or template answer)

tokens_in.description: not recorded by the ledger today: null

DebugRead.description:
A developer-facing reading of the day, written from the structured data above. Gemma's when `by` is gemma
(every claim cites facts, every number is one of theirs); otherwise the same shape written by code. It never
changes the consensus.

attempts.description: model calls this ask made (0 = the model was not asked)

digest.description: hash of the read version, the instruction, rule version, model and the day's data

est_usd.description: the spend ledger's estimate for the ask: its rows for this task and model while the ask ran

failed.description: the model was asked about exactly this day's data and nothing valid came back; kept with its reason and rejections until the day's data, the rule or the instruction changes, and not asked (or paid for) again before that

fallback_reason.description: why the deterministic read is shown: not_requested | provider_unavailable | over_budget | invalid_json | no_valid_claims | cooldown

latency_ms.description: how long the ask took, all attempts together

moved.description: which measures moved, and by how much

reading.description: by code, from the day's metrics: never the model's call

rejected.description: validator category -> claims dropped, over all attempts of the ask

rule_check.description: whether the rule's answer looks right

tomorrow.description: what would change the state tomorrow

DebugRead.title: DebugRead

DebugVerdict.description: One signal group's verdict that day with what made it.

days_with_data.description: in the baseline window up to that day

insufficient_reason.description: only when the verdict is insufficient, in the rule's own order: stale = nothing newer than the group's max_age_days; low_confidence = confidence below min_confidence; no_usable_metric = no scored measure has a usable baseline and no rule fired

worse_weight.description: sum of the weights of its drifting metrics

DebugVerdict.title: DebugVerdict

baseline_lag_days.description: baseline ends this many days before today, so a slow drift doesn't drag its own baseline along

drift_days.description: drifting if beyond threshold on >= drift_days ...

drift_window.description: ... of the last drift_window available days

early_baseline_lag_days.description: lag of that provisional baseline (shorter than baseline_lag_days, so the first days can be compared at all)

early_baseline_min_days.description: 0 = off. While a metric's record is younger than baseline_days + baseline_lag_days and has no full baseline yet, use a provisional baseline from at least this many days

min_mad.description: noise floor for MAD in metric units (avoids huge z on flat data)

quality_min.description: ignore readings with envelope.quality below this

rule_max_age_days.description: [[rule]] observations older than this no longer fire

force_mean.description: None when the drum can't sense force (KY-031 knock switch)

rejected_taps.description: double-triggers dropped by the refractory window

taps_per_s.description: energy proxy that needs no force sensor

tempo_end_bpm.description: tempo of the last third of the taps

tempo_start_bpm.description: tempo of the first third of the taps

Engagement.description:
Robot ritual, once at the end and only when the person accepted the conversation: a deterministic summary of
how animated the session was, fused from every available cue (face presence + movement from box positions,
speech pace/pauses, drum energy, pulse, dial answers, steps completed). No single cue decides and the face share
is capped; fewer than 2 cues -> `level` is None. It is an observation feature with provenance: not an emotion,
not a diagnosis, and it feeds no verdict. Computed from numbers only; no image or audio is stored or sent.

agreement.description: 1 - spread of the available cue levels

Engagement.title: Engagement

EngagementCue.description: One cue of the robot's engagement summary. `available: false` = missing evidence (never a zero score).

basis.description: what it was computed from, or why it is missing

level.description: 0-1 on a fixed reference range, not a baseline

EngagementCue.title: EngagementCue

EpisodeIn.description:
POST /v1/companion/episode — one finished session (also for sessions run offline). Never audio.
`transcript` only when the person opted in (device consent `transcripts`, off by default); the cloud drops it
if the outcome is `crisis` or any turn matches a crisis phrase.

transcript.description: opt-in only; person-facing + deletable; never on a clinician route; de-identified for training

EpisodeIn.title: EpisodeIn

EvalResult.description: Simulation on synthetic patients with known onset. Not clinical accuracy.

ablation.description: needs_call score with one source removed

EvalResult.title: EvalResult

Explanation.description: Plain-language explanation of a consensus. Gemma or template. An explanation, not a decision.
Explanation.title: Explanation

FaceSigns.description:
Face signs during one task (D52), with the person's opt-in "Camera during activities": movements of the face
that the phone's or Mac's own camera could count while a game or the check-in chat ran. One per task session in
which the camera sampled. Frames are looked at in memory on that device and never stored or sent; only these
numbers leave it. They are observable movements (smiles, brows, blinks, mouth, gaze, head, range of expression),
not emotions: nothing here says what the person felt, and no field may. Values are comparable only within one
`method` (and best within one task): never pool the two methods into one usual. A sign the method cannot
measure is None, never a zero: the landmark method sends no smile, brow or gaze sign, and blinks, head movement
and expression range come from both methods on different scales. The apps also leave out blinks under 20 s of
face time, head movement under 2 s and expression range under 10 face frames, and send nothing at all when
coverage rounds to 0. A record with `coverage` 0 is still valid here (provenance only) and carries no sign.
Counts toward the "laptop" (display: Apps) group beside the task; config/criteria.toml reads it as shown, not
scored.

blinks_per_min.description: blinks per minute of face time

brow_furrow_share.description: share of face frames with lowered, drawn brows

brow_raise_share.description: share of face frames with raised brows

coverage.description: share of sampled frames with exactly one usable face

expression_range.description: overall variability of expression over the session

gaze_on_share.description: share of face frames looking toward the screen

head_movement.description: how much the head moved; the scale belongs to the method

method.description: arkit_blendshapes: TrueDepth face tracking coefficients (iPhone); vision_landmarks: 2-D face landmarks (Mac, other iPhones)

mouth_open_share.description: share of face frames with the mouth open

ref.description: id of the obs.play_session (or other record) of the same task

samples.description: frames looked at; none is kept

smile_share.description: share of face frames with a smile above the method's threshold

task.description: the task it belongs to: a game (PlayGame) or the check-in chat

FaceSigns.title: FaceSigns

FeelPlan.description:
Result of the `feel` tool: how to meet what the person just shared. Chosen by code from this person's own
record; hints for the companion's own words, never a script. Nothing here is a state or changes one.

depth.description: brief: an ordinary moment, the chat may stay small. stay: a strong feeling either way, repeated heaviness, or they keep talking: never close first

follow_up_saved.description: a thread to ask about next time was kept

manner.description: a words-only cue for how to carry yourself in this conversation (go more gently), never something to say, and never a number, a state or where the cue came from (D52)

may_offer.description: one small thing to offer once, or null

offer_activity.description: start_activity kind, only after a clear yes

offer_elsewhere.description: the offer has no screen on this device but one on their phone or Mac: after a clear yes call agree_activity with this kind (D50)

offer_note.description: why that one, and how to offer it

recall.description: one thing the record knows that fits

scheduling.description: Live FunctionResponse scheduling for this non-blocking tool: send it as `response.scheduling` so the model answers with the plan as soon as it is idle

FeelPlan.title: FeelPlan

Garden.description:
Reward only (no data). plants = finished interactions in the last 14 days; resting after 3 quiet days.
It never wilts and there is no streak counter. `days` = the last 14 local days, oldest first (one plot each).
Garden.title: Garden

GardenDay.description:
One plot of the garden: what was done together that local day (kinds: ritual, drum_session, play_session,
outing, friend_link, weather_check). A quiet day is an empty plot, never a wilted one.
GardenDay.title: GardenDay

evidence.description: how many observations / sessions / memories back this node

id.description: graph node id; negative = derived for this view (routines, obs-only activities)

trend.description: this week vs the week before across this group's measures

sufficient.description: enough recent usable data for this group to give a verdict

HeadCmd.description:
Robot face + body, all on the Atech head node: eyes/look (Color Display), chest/color/bpm (LED grids),
pan/home/gesture (pan motor, hall homing), purr (speaker tone; no purr motor on the current build).

drum.description: only for a head that runs its own ritual (standalone firmware): hold = the hub runs the drum phase now (stay in the drum step, keep reporting taps, no own timer, obey eyes / pan_mode sway / bpm); end = it is over, go on. Re-sent at least every 5 s; 10 s without one = back to the head's own timer. Ignored by a hub-driven head

gesture.description: timed motor pulse, then home (no position feedback)

mic.description: open = send the head's microphone as PCM frames on audio/head/mic (only while a conversation the person started is open); close = stop. Re-sent at least every 3 s; the head closes by itself after 10 s without one. Half-duplex: no frames while its speaker plays and about 250 ms after

show.description: help = the head shows the helpline's name and number and the emergency number on its own screen, from constants compiled into the firmware, until `none`, a new ritual, or 10 minutes; never a sound. Sent by the hub's crisis path only

HeadCmd.title: HeadCmd

HealthOverview.description: GET /v1/health — every home's last NodeHealthReport, for the /health page.
HealthOverview.title: HealthOverview

HeardTone.description:
How a conversation sounded to the model that was in it, reported through the `feel` tool. An observation
by a model, never a measurement and never a state. `model_heard`: the native-audio voice model heard the
person speak. `model_read`: it went by their typed or transcribed words only.

moments.description: how many times a feeling was noticed in that conversation

HeardTone.title: HeardTone

HelpEffect.description: What the learner has seen for one activity. A reported response, not proof that the activity caused it.
HelpEffect.title: HelpEffect

Highlight.description: One line for "Your days": a good moment or a gentle note about a harder day. Plain, friendly, never clinical.
Highlight.title: Highlight

HistoryDay.description: One local day of one measure.

sessions.description: readings that day that the value is made from

sim.description: some of that day's readings are simulated

HistoryDay.title: HistoryDay

HistoryMeasure.description: One measure over the window: its days, the person's usual range when there is one, and its latest sessions.

days.description: days with a value, oldest first; a day without data is absent

decimals.description: how many decimals the value is worth showing with

devices.description: where its readings came from in this window, most first (head, sensors and hub are all the robot)

format.description: clock: minutes after local midnight; percent: a share 0..1 shown as a percentage; duration: minutes shown as hours and minutes. `usual` is in the same format

key.description: stable key; for a measure the practitioner side also computes, the same name

per_day.description: how one day's value is made from that day's sessions

HistoryMeasure.title: HistoryMeasure

HistorySession.description:
One recorded session (a drum session, one game, a breathing round, a walk, one dial answer, one morning's
watch summary) with its own numbers.

label.description: which kind of session, where one measure lists several (a ritual step: Breathing, Drumming)

warmup.description: games: a practice session, left out of the day's value

HistorySession.title: HistorySession

HistoryUsual.description: The person's own usual range for a measure, from their own earlier days. A range and nothing else.
HistoryUsual.title: HistoryUsual

HistoryValue.description: One number of one session, ready to show.
HistoryValue.title: HistoryValue

method.description: finger = KY-039 cradle (HR + RMSSD); camera = forehead-green backup (HR only, never RMSSD: ~15 Hz is too coarse for beat-to-beat timing)

phq9_due.description: ask PHQ-9 in the next ritual (spoken mode)

HubTrace.description:
`raw.hub.trace`: what Kaiku just did, live, for the "Kaiku bot" tab of the person's own apps on the home
network. Local only (raw.* never leaves the home; QoS 0, not retained, not stored). It carries Kaiku's OWN
lines and the names of the tools the voice called. Never the person's words, a system instruction, or a tool's
arguments or result: `text` exists for `said` alone and `heard` carries nothing but its kind (validated).

bpm.description: music song / game level: its tempo

by.description: said: how it was spoken (script | live | cached_voice). tool: who answered, only when the cloud's result says so

detail.description: a short machine word. session: open | close. music: start | song | hush | stop. game: level:<n> | your_turn | band:<perfect|great|nice|again>

ms.description: tool: how long the call took

text.description: said only: Kaiku's own words (a scripted line, or the Live voice's reply as its output transcription gives it), cut at 300 characters

tool.description: tool only: the name of the tool the voice called

HubTrace.title: HubTrace

InsightChange.description: One thing that is different on a day, pointing at its node. Text and order are written by code.

tag.description: where it sits in the order of the change, when the course has one: 'first to move', '1 day after the first change' (order in time, never cause)

InsightChange.title: InsightChange

InsightDomain.description:
A neighbourhood of the graph: what a group of nodes is about, and where it sits around the person. Declared
once in config/kaiku.toml [graph]; the same for every person.
InsightDomain.title: InsightDomain

on.description: the days this link is about, oldest first: the day a measure followed, the days two measures were away together, the day it came back

tag.description: a few words for a badge: '+1 day', 'first'

InsightGraph.description:
What a practitioner may see of what Kaiku has learned: signal groups, measures, observed activities, routines
and what helped. Built from observations; conversation counts join only when the person shares. Never people,
places, likes, plans, memories or transcripts.

days.description: every calendar day from the first to the last day with data inside the graph's window, oldest first

shared.description: the person shares conversation-derived activity counts with the care team

InsightGraph.title: InsightGraph

InsightGraphDay.description: One day of the graph's record: what changed that day and how many measures were away from usual.

away.description: measures away from their usual that day

recorded.description: at least one observation or care action that day

InsightGraphDay.title: InsightGraphDay

domain.description: id of the `InsightGraph.domains` entry this node is about; empty for the person and the signal groups (who sent it is not what it is about)

evidence.description: recorded days / observations / attempts behind this node

layer.description: learned = found in this person's record; structure = how the record is organised

InsightNodeDay.description:
What one graph node has on one day of the record, by the same code as the course, the trends band and the
daily account. A day with nothing for the node has no entry.

text.description: one plain clause by code: '2 of 5, below their usual 4 of 5'

tone.description: measure: that day's reading against that day's own usual (worse = away from usual, better = beyond usual on the favourable side, similar = within usual, unknown = no personal usual yet); routine: similar = kept, worse = missed on a recorded day; every other kind: unknown (recorded, not judged)

InsightNodeDay.title: InsightNodeDay

IntelligenceHealth.description:
GET /v1/health/intelligence — usage ledger summary (no content is ever logged): which models ran, how often,
how fast, how often we fell back. `routes` counts ask_mind outcomes (memory/flash/argon/fallback).
IntelligenceHealth.title: IntelligenceHealth

InterventionResponse.description: Immediate before/after effect of one activity (feeds the bandit learner).
InterventionResponse.title: InterventionResponse

Invitation.description:
One thing Kaiku would like to bring up or offer now. Chosen by code; `text` is a template from
config/voice_lines.toml (`voice_key`) around the person's own stored words. On yes the device opens Talk
(kind talk_about: the session card already carries the thread) or the screen for `activity`.

id.description: send it back in the answer; an answered item is never offered again

voice_key.description: the template used; speak `text` with POST /v1/voice/say

Invitation.title: Invitation

InvitationAnswer.description: POST /v1/me/invitation/answer — yes: the device opens it. not_now: final. Either way the item is settled.
InvitationAnswer.title: InvitationAnswer

InvitationResponse.description:
GET /v1/me/invitation — at most one invitation a day per home; null when there is nothing to offer, when
today's was answered, or on an extra-gentle day with nothing to talk about.

agreed.description: what the person said yes to today, on any device (D50), oldest first. While one is open or started the invitation waits (`invitation` is null)

InvitationResponse.title: InvitationResponse

KnowledgeGraph.title: KnowledgeGraph

LaptopSession.description:
2-minute laptop session. All features computed in the browser; nothing recorded.
Any feature may be None if that part was skipped or unsupported (e.g. no webcam).
LaptopSession.title: LaptopSession

LastReflection.description: How the latest talk with Kaiku went: a level and themes, never the words.

declined.description: they did not want to talk or asked to stop

LastReflection.title: LastReflection

caveat.description: how far the reported responses can be trusted

LiveEventsResponse.description: GET /v1/events?home_id=&since=&limit= — recent obs for the /live page.
LiveEventsResponse.title: LiveEventsResponse

LiveToken.description:
Gemini Live ephemeral token: use `token` as the API key for ONE Live session (v1beta). Start within
`new_session_expires_at`; the session may run until `expires_at`.
LiveToken.title: LiveToken

Mascot.description:
Kaiku's ambient mood (plan 02 §2): a pure function of the consensus state, computed once in the cloud so every
surface shows the same thing. Never sad or worried at the person: stable -> idle/happy, watch -> cozy,
needs_call -> cozy + the nurse-chat offer, safety -> "crisis" (clients show the scripted crisis screen from
config/safety_phrases.toml: no animation, no character lines; line_key is then null).
Mascot.title: Mascot

MeResponse.description: Person-facing view. Plain language, never alarming.
MeResponse.title: MeResponse

MemoriesResponse.description: GET /v1/me/memories — "What Kaiku remembers". Person-facing only; no clinician route returns memories.

remember.description: false = the person turned remembering off

MemoriesResponse.title: MemoriesResponse

MetricComparison.description: One measure: this week vs the week before vs the person's own usual. Medians of recorded days.

early_baseline.description: the usual is a provisional baseline of a young record

sustained.description: the rule engine's reading over recent days (criteria thresholds), not a one-week difference

usual.description: personal baseline median for the latest scored day

MetricComparison.title: MetricComparison

scored.description: false = shown and citable against the person's usual, never part of the group's verdict (criteria `role = "shown"`, or weight 0)

at_least.description: payload minimums: a reading counts only when each named numeric payload field is at least this (e.g. coverage, samples). The record is still stored and listed with its provenance

day_field.description: payload ISO date used for daily grouping; envelope timestamp orders snapshots

family.description: e.g. self_report | physiology | behaviour | voice | cognition

field.description: payload field (nested with a dot, e.g. category_min.communication), or @count / @local_minutes

missing.description: days without data: ignore, or count as 0 (sum/count metrics)

person_hard.description: plain, gentle sentence shown to the PERSON on /me ('Your days') for a day this metric was beyond the usual in its worse direction; empty = never shown. Wording rules: root AGENTS.md (no clinical words)

role.description: shown = compared with the person's usual, charted and citable, never part of a verdict (no vote, no sufficiency, no coverage) and not in the rule version. Delete the line to let the metric vote with its weight

weight.description: counts toward the source's worse/better weight

MindAnswer.description:
`result` of the `ask_mind` tool (CompanionToolResult.result). `answer` is ready to say: citation tags are
verified and stripped by code. `ask_person=true`: Kaiku found conflicting notes and should ask, not pick.
`route`: memory = answered by code (no model) · flash · argon · fallback = scripted hand-off line.
MindAnswer.title: MindAnswer

NextStep.description: A suggested next step for the care team, chosen by fixed rules (never a model). Allowed wording only.

action.description: the dashboard action that does it, if any

NextStep.title: NextStep

NodeHealthReport.description: PUT /v1/health/{home_id} — hub reports its nodes' heartbeats (derived status only).
NodeHealthReport.title: NodeHealthReport

captured_by.description: envelope sources that sent it (hub, phone, …)

simulated.description: how many of these observations carry sim=true

Outing.description:
A walk / time outdoors. Everything is computed on the phone / glasses; only these numbers are uplinked.

daylight_min only with a camera (DAT camera app or the iPhone DAT bridge: sparse frames -> brightness, frames
discarded). cadence / gait / head-up come from the glasses IMU via the DAT SDK (`method: dat_imu`, beta).

head_up_ratio.description: share of walking time looking ahead/up

Outing.title: Outing

PatientInsight.description:
GET /v1/patients/{id}/insight — everything the intelligence layer knows that a practitioner may see, in one
payload: Gemma's evidence-cited review, the steps that produced it, week-over-week comparison, the learned
routine, the permitted graph and data coverage. State comes from the deterministic consensus only.

day_of_record.description: calendar days since the first observation

early_record.description: provisional or missing baselines: lower confidence

state_history.description: oldest first, one row per day replayed

status_line.description: one statement by code that reconciles the rule state with the course: when it was raised, what has come back, why it still shows

PatientInsight.title: PatientInsight

PatientReview.description: Gemma's review of the person: what changed, what it likely means, what to consider. Never decides state.

day_of_record.description: calendar days since the first observation

early_record.description: baselines are provisional or missing: read every comparison with lower confidence

fallback_reason.description: content-free category when the template answered instead of the model, e.g. not_requested | provider_unavailable | invalid_json | no_valid_findings | cooldown

overview.description: Gemma's reading of the whole record: what started, what followed, what has come back, what has not. Null when the template answered; `PatientInsight.course.summary` is the code-written arc

overview_cites.description: evidence ids the overview rests on

PatientReview.title: PatientReview

PatientsResponse.description: Ranked: safety, needs_call, watch, stable (see STATE_RANK).
PatientsResponse.title: PatientsResponse

back_in_range.description: metric names back within usual after a spell

changed.description: metric names worse than the week before

early_baseline.description: at least one usual here is a provisional baseline

improved.description: metric names better than the week before

since_low.description: against the spell's low point, e.g. '12 of 18 measures back within usual since the low on 8 Nov'; empty when nothing moved

still_away.description: metric names still away from usual

PersonHistory.description:
GET /v1/me/history?home_id=&days= — the person's own numbers, as a health app shows them: every measure
the home has produced, from every device, by local day, with the latest sessions one tap away. Groups come in
a fixed order (robot, games, walks, checkins, sleep_body, mac, camera); a group or measure with no data in the
window is left out. `camera` holds the face signs counted with "Camera during activities" on (D52): her own
numbers like every other group, never a word for what they might mean. It is the one person-facing place where numbers are shown (D48), and it carries numbers only:
never a state, a verdict, a score against the usual, a flag, a weight, a direction word, anything from the
practitioner's review, a safety flag or a questionnaire answer.
PersonHistory.title: PersonHistory

Phq9.description: PHQ-9 (every 14 days). items[8] is item 9; > 0 triggers the safety path.
Phq9.title: Phq9

PlaySession.description:
One short game with Kaiku (firefly go/no-go, breathe, tell-Kaiku, pebbles memory span) on the phone, Mac or
web. Every feature is
computed on the device; no audio, video or transcript is stored or sent. Fields a game doesn't produce are None.
Counts toward the "laptop" (display: Apps) source wherever it was played.

accuracy.description: pebbles: share of taps that were right; seeds: share of answers right

camera_face_coverage.description: fraction of sampled frames containing one usable face

camera_samples.description: number of sampled camera frames; frames are never stored

expressivity_index.description: optional local facial movement variability; not an emotion or wellbeing score

face_movement.description: optional normalised face position movement during the task

false_starts.description: lantern: taps before the light or faster than 100 ms

hard_choice_ratio.description: watering: share of rounds the bigger, harder plant was chosen

input.description: how the person answered (provenance for timing)

lapses.description: firefly: responses > 500 ms or missed fireflies

reaction_ms_cv.description: lantern: SD / mean of valid RTs

response_speed.description: lantern: mean of 1000 / RT ms over valid trials (1/s)

rt_ms.description: per-trial response time in order, ms (0 = no response); the compact raw data behind the summary numbers

session_index.description: nth finished session of this game on this device (1 = first)

trial_codes.description: one character per trial, same order as rt_ms. lantern: h hit, l lapse (>= 500 ms), m missed, a anticipation; seeds: c correct, x wrong; watering: H hard chosen, E easy chosen (lowercase = not finished in time)

valid.description: false when the validity rules failed (see flags); the envelope quality is then < 0.5 so the metric skips it

warmup.description: true for the first sessions of a game on a device (practice effects): criteria metrics filter warmup = false

PlaySession.title: PlaySession

finds.description: light-hunt finds as short words, e.g. 'green', 'bird'

PostcardResponse.description:
POST /v1/companion/postcard — an illustrated walk postcard (no photos, no faces). 503 + {detail, reason,
hint} when image generation is unavailable: the app shows its own static card.

url.description: GET this path for the image

PostcardResponse.title: PostcardResponse

RawFace.description: Face position only. Images are never published, stored or transmitted.
RawFace.title: RawFace

force.description: peak acceleration, g; None for a knock switch

heard.description: as reported by the model in the conversation

ReflectionOverview.description:
Reflections with Kaiku at summary level: how many sounded low / neutral / bright and what they were about.
Present only when the person shares with the care team. Never their words.

declined.description: the person asked to stop or did not want to talk

reflections.description: reflections with a summary in the last 7 days

summary.description: the fortnight in one or two sentences; counts are 7 days

themes.description: theme -> reflections it came up in

tone_summary.description: how they sounded, by provenance: tone of their words, and tone as reported by the model in the conversation

ReflectionOverview.title: ReflectionOverview

ReviewFinding.description:
One claim in the review. `meaning`/`consider` are interpretation (Gemma when `by` = gemma: validated, no
numbers, no state words); `facts` are rendered by code from the cited records and carry every number.

facts.description: verified record facts, numbers rendered by code

meaning.description: what it likely means, in plain words

ReviewFinding.title: ReviewFinding

Routine.description: A rhythm found BY CODE in the last weeks (obs, and conversations for the person or when shared).

activity.description: ritual | walk | drum | breathe | checkin | laptop | play | sleep

this_week.description: days with it in the last 7 days

usual_time.description: local HH:MM (median of the usual weeks)

Routine.title: Routine

RuleSpec.description: A direct trigger: when it fires, the metric's source counts as 'worse' regardless of baselines.

kind.description: at_least: value >= threshold · at_most: value <= threshold · rise/drop_vs_previous: change vs the previous observation >= threshold

RuleSpec.title: RuleSpec

ScreenActivity.description:
Usage rhythm (D26), one per period (hourly) from the Mac app. Computed on the Mac from the frontmost app's
bundle id + idle time only: no window titles, URLs, keystrokes or screenshots ever leave it (or are kept).
`paused: true` = the person paused sensing for (part of) this period; the numbers then cover the rest only.

period_min.description: length of the period this summarises (60 = hourly)

ScreenActivity.title: ScreenActivity

ScreenCategoryMinutes.description: Minutes by broad category, from a LOCAL bundle-id -> category table on the Mac. Never titles/URLs/content.
ScreenCategoryMinutes.title: ScreenCategoryMinutes

SelfReport.description: One dial answer (turn the ear). The ritual asks mood, energy, last night's sleep.

channel.description: where the dial was answered: robot ear, phone/Mac/web weather check, or spoken on the glasses (parsed on the phone, no transcript kept). Always counts toward the robot source

scale_10.description: the answer exactly as dialled when the device has a 1-10 dial (the standalone robot head); `value` is then ceil(scale_10 / 2). Absent for 1-5 dials

SelfReport.title: SelfReport

chime.description: short cue on the Modulino Buzzer; alert = device fault only

SessionClose.description:
POST /v1/companion/close — the device says a conversation stopped and how long it ran. The cloud never
sees the audio socket, so this is what brings the Live budget reservation down to the time really used
(whole started minutes, at least one, never more than was reserved). Send it once when the conversation
ends, whatever ended it; sending it again is harmless. It changes nothing else about the session.

elapsed_s.description: seconds from the conversation's start to its end, across every token it used

SessionClose.title: SessionClose

billed_minutes.description: started minutes now counted for this conversation

settled.description: Live reservations this call settled or corrected (0: nothing to change)

better_min_weight.description: sum of improving-metric weights needed for 'better'

expected_per_week.description: days with data per week expected (confidence)

max_age_days.description: latest qualifying observation older than this -> insufficient

worse_min_weight.description: sum of drifting-metric weights needed for 'worse'

SourceWeek.description: What one source added to the record in the last 7 days (counts only, no content).
SourceWeek.title: SourceWeek

SpeechFeatures.description: Robot-side speech features from the local mic. No audio, no transcript.
SpeechFeatures.title: SpeechFeatures

StateDay.description: The deterministic consensus replayed for one day of the record.

early.description: fewer days on record than min_history_days_for_stable: never stable yet

StateDay.title: StateDay

correlated_families.description: if every 'worse' source is worse only via one of these families, add the independence caveat

count_correlated_as_one.description: if true, sources worse only via the same correlated family count as ONE worse source

hysteresis_stable_days.description: needs_call holds until acknowledged or N stable days

min_history_days_for_stable.description: 0 = off. A record with fewer calendar days than this can never be 'stable' (the personal baseline is still forming): it reads 'watch' with agreement low_coverage

min_sufficient_for_stable.description: fewer sufficient sources can never be 'stable'

watch_if_single_sufficient.description: only one source has enough data -> watch

StreamAgreed.description:
SSE `event: agreed` — an agreed activity appeared or changed. Ids and kinds only: read the sentence with
GET /v1/me/invitation. `open`: just agreed (show it, post the notification). `removed`: it is gone (take the
card and any pending notification away).
StreamAgreed.title: StreamAgreed

StreamDay.description:
SSE `event: day` — new observations were stored for this home: what a screen shows about today may have
changed (a check-in on the robot, a walk, a game). Types and senders only, never a value.

day.description: the local day the newest of them belongs to

StreamDay.title: StreamDay

StreamHello.description:
GET /v1/me/stream, first frame of every connection (SSE `event: hello`, no id). `resync: true`: the
`Last-Event-ID` the client sent could not be continued (another process, or too long ago), so events may
have been missed: read `/v1/me`, `/v1/me/invitation` and whatever else the screen shows again.

heartbeat_s.description: a `ping` at least this often; no frame for well over twice this long means the connection is dead: reconnect with Last-Event-ID

last_id.description: id of the newest event for this home, if any

replayed.description: events sent again right after this frame

StreamHello.title: StreamHello

StreamInvitation.description: SSE `event: invitation` — today's invitation was answered on some device: take its card away.
StreamInvitation.title: StreamInvitation

TapBack.description:
Robot rhythm game "Tap it back" (D51): Kaiku plays a short song, it goes quiet, she taps its beat from memory.
The tempo is given to her, so this is NOT her own spontaneous tempo (that is obs.drum_session) and no metric in
config/criteria.toml reads it: it is stored for her own History and feeds no verdict.

duration_s.description: from the first song to the last band

error_pct.description: mean over the levels that have a tapped tempo

levels_passed.description: levels whose band is nice, great or perfect

rejected_taps.description: double-triggers dropped by the refractory window

song.description: how the tempo was given: generated music, the hub's own plain beat, or the head's light only

steadiness.description: mean over the levels that have one

TapBack.title: TapBack

TapBackLevel.description: One level of Tap it back: the song's tempo and the try that counted (the closer one when a level was replayed).

beat.description: half / double = she tapped every other beat, or two to a beat, and was compared with that

error_pct.description: |tapped - target| / target x 100, against the beat level named in `beat`; None with no tempo

steadiness.description: 1 - spread of the gaps between taps

tapped_bpm.description: median gap between her taps as a tempo; None = too few taps to call one

target_bpm.description: the tempo of the song Kaiku played

tries.description: times the level was played (1 = no replay)

TapBackLevel.title: TapBackLevel

face_signs.description: obs.face_signs of the same window, newest first (D52): `payload.ref` names the task session each belongs to. Movements counted on the device; never an emotion

early.description: this day's baseline is a provisional one of a young record

Transcript.description: One stored conversation (opt-in). Person-facing only: no clinician route returns transcripts.
Transcript.title: Transcript

complete.description: true when transcription explicitly finished; false when interrupted/not final; null or absent for unknown legacy status. Audio turnComplete does not establish transcription completion.

TranscriptsResponse.description: GET /v1/me/transcripts — the person's own stored conversations, newest first.
TranscriptsResponse.title: TranscriptsResponse

VoiceLinesResponse.description:
GET /v1/voice?lang= — every keyed line Kaiku says (config/voice_lines.toml), for captions and offline use.
Audio for one line: GET /v1/voice/{line_key}?lang= (audio/wav, cached; 503 + JSON hint without a TTS key).
VoiceLinesResponse.title: VoiceLinesResponse

VoiceSayRequest.description:
POST /v1/voice/say — any short line (not in voice_lines.toml) in Kaiku's one voice → audio/wav. Cached by
(model, voice, lang, text, style); home token required. A crisis phrase in `text` → 422 (the crisis script is
shown verbatim, never voiced from here).
VoiceSayRequest.title: VoiceSayRequest

WalkGoalResult.description: What the device returns for `set_walk_goal`: the count it keeps.
WalkGoalResult.title: WalkGoalResult

WalkGuide.description:
CompanionSessionResponse.walk: how the device keeps a walk going. A Live session only answers input, so the
device nudges: it sends `look_prompt` as a context text turn every `look_every_s` while the camera is on and
nobody is speaking, and `quiet_prompt` once after `quiet_after_s` without anyone speaking. Null = that nudge
is not used in this style. Values: config/kaiku.toml [walk].
Kaiku answers a nudge in words only when there is something to say. A declined nudge has no words but is not
always silent (real sessions: often a second or two of non-speech sound, transcribed `<no speech>` or `×`),
so the device holds the audio of a nudge's reply until its first output transcription fragment and plays it
only when that fragment has a real word.
WalkGuide.title: WalkGuide

WalkMomentResult.description:
What the device returns for `log_walk_moment` (one find). Without a goal: ok=true, the counts null, and
`note` tells the model that nothing was counted and to call `set_walk_goal` first, then log the find again.

note.description: for the model, when there was no goal to count against

WalkMomentResult.title: WalkMomentResult

WearableDaily.description:
Daily summary from Apple Health (HealthKit) on the iPhone: Apple Watch or any watch that writes to Apple Health.
Posted once per morning; `date` = that local morning: sleep = the night that ended this morning, steps /
exercise / resting HR / HRV = the previous 24 h. Only these aggregates leave the phone (no raw samples).
Optional source: people without a watch simply never send it.

daylight_min.description: time in daylight over the previous day, minutes (Apple Watch only; absent otherwise)

distance_km.description: walking + running distance over the previous day (00:00 to 00:00 local, the window of steps), km

sleep_awake_min.description: minutes awake between first falling asleep and the last waking; absent when the source wrote none

sleep_core_min.description: minutes of core sleep last night

sleep_deep_min.description: minutes of deep sleep last night; the three stages are sent together or not at all (0 allowed)

sleep_midpoint_min.description: midpoint of last night's sleep, minutes from local midnight (-30 = 23:30, 210 = 03:30)

sleep_rem_min.description: minutes of REM sleep last night

walking_hr_bpm.description: average walking heart rate over the previous day

WearableDaily.title: WearableDaily

metric.description: criteria metric name this rests on

WeekSummary.description:
GET /v1/me/week (person wording) · GET /v1/patients/{id}/week (care team). Derived deterministically from
obs, per-metric drift against the person's own usual, the bandit and (person / shared only) conversations.
No model decides anything here; it never changes the consensus.

shared.description: the person shares what Kaiku learned with the care team

sources.description: the one record: what each source added

WeekSummary.title: WeekSummary
